action: Do not administer ARNi to patients with history of angioedema
action_detail: ARNi should not be administered to patients with any history of angioedema due to the concern that it will increase the risk of recurrence. Angioedema was an exclusion criterion in PARADIGM-HF. Rates of angioedema were numerically higher with ARNi vs ACEi.
source_text: ARNi should not be administered to patients with any history of angioedema. (Class III: Harm, LOE C-LD)

action: Do not administer ACEi to patients with history of angioedema
action_detail: ACEi should not be administered to patients with any history of angioedema. Angioedema attributable to ACEi results from defective degradation of bradykinin, des-Arg9-BK, and substance P. ARB may be used as an alternative as they do not interfere as directly with bradykinin metabolism.
source_text: ACEi should not be administered to patients with any history of angioedema. (Class III: Harm, LOE C-LD)

action: Do not administer ARNi concomitantly with ACEi or within 36 hours of last ACEi dose
action_detail: Oral neprilysin inhibitors combined with ACEi can lead to angioedema. Both ACEi and neprilysin break down bradykinin, and dual inhibition causes unacceptable incidence of angioedema. A 36-hour washout period is required when switching between ACEi and ARNi.

properties.mechanism: dual bradykinin degradation inhibition causing angioedema risk

source_text: ARNi should not be administered concomitantly with ACEi or within 36 hours of the last dose of an ACEi. (Class III: Harm, LOE B-R)
